name: Slow Cooker Boneless Beef Short Ribs

prose.intro_html: Short ribs have a reputation as special-occasion food, the kind of thing you order out and pay restaurant money for. The boneless ones tell a different story. Give them a few hours in a slow cooker with a can of fire roasted tomatoes and they turn fork-tender on their own, no browning, no fuss, no standing at the stove. This is about as close to free time as cooking gets: five things go in the crock, you walk away, and dinner for the whole week is waiting when you come back. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. That is a rich, slow-braised beef dinner that does not fight your macros or your wallet.
shop_smart: Seven pounds of boneless short ribs is the anchor. This is the cut that eats like a braise but skips the bone you would pay for and then throw away. Buy the family pack when the case has it rather than the little trays, because you are paying for beef, not packaging. This is where most of the money and all of the protein live.

Fire roasted diced tomatoes do the work of a sauce. You want the canned kind with their juices, and the fire roasted label brings a little smoke that plain tomatoes miss. Poured over the top they cook down into the braising liquid, so there is no stock to buy and no gravy to make. Plain diced tomatoes work in a pinch if the fire roasted are not on the shelf.

Onion, garlic, and thyme are the whole seasoning. A little chopped onion and minced garlic go on top of the meat, and a couple teaspoons of dried thyme tie it to the beef. These are backbone pantry items you buy once and cook with all week, and they are what keep this from tasting like plain pot roast.

Salt and pepper are the only thing left. Season the ribs on both sides before they go in and taste again at the end. That is the entire shopping list, which is the whole point of a five ingredient dinner.
make_it: Weigh your empty slow cooker insert and write the number down. You will need it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which is the only honest way to portion one big braise.
Season the short ribs on both sides with salt and pepper, then lay them in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Scatter the minced garlic, the dried thyme, and the chopped onion over the meat, then pour the fire roasted diced tomatoes and their juices over the top so everything is covered.
Put the lid on and cook on high for 4 hours or on low for 8 hours, until the short ribs are fork-tender and pull apart with light pressure.
Break the meat into big chunks and stir it through the tomatoes and juices so every piece is coated, then weigh the insert and portion as below.
prose.portion_html: Set the full insert on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total, meat and juices together. Divide that number by 14 and spoon that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for slow-braised short ribs that most people think of as a night out. The beef and the tomatoes carry the whole thing. Spoon it over cauliflower rice or a pile of greens and you have a full plate that never saw the inside of a restaurant.
